events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The trace fixes the branch: cancelled_by = rider on this immediate booking [F2], so the case enters through NS-0 and is governed by NS-4. The trace marks NS-4 as failed — the rider cancelled 175 s (2 min 55 s) after acceptance, inside the 3-minute free-cancellation window [F2]. Under NS-4 a rider cancellation within 3:00 of matching is not chargeable, so the $6.61 fee on record [F5] has no basis.

The driver's own conduct confirms this is not a no-show case: the platform never recorded him at the pickup point [F3], he never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was recorded [F4], and his closest approach was 2189 m — never inside 200 m [F1]. The NS-1 conditions (i)(ii)(iii) therefore cannot be satisfied, and NS-2's consequence of a full $6.61 refund to the rider follows [F1][F3][F4][NS-2]. NS-3 likewise places no cancellation fee on the rider when the driver does not establish a rider no-show [F3][F4][NS-3].

Amount: the disputed item is the cancellation fee of $6.61 [F5], refunded in full; no per-km computation applies because there is no off-route segment and no metered distance fare in this case [F5][RD-2].

The driver's statement that he "was on his way" [F10] is a mere assertion and, in any event, is irrelevant: under NS-4 the driver not having arrived is not a ground for the rider to be charged — the rider's protection is the 3-minute window itself [F2][F10][NS-4]. The mild congestion on Stevens Road (band 4, 30–39 km/h) and the absence of incidents or weather issues [F11][F12][F13] concern the driver's ETA, which NS-8 confirms is not a cancellation-fee element in Ryde's policy [F8][NS-4].

No profile fact decides anything here: neither party has an upheld dispute in the last 90 days [F14][F15], so RD-6 is not engaged and no account flag arises [F14][F15][RD-6]. NS-7's 30-day dispute window is met (complaint filed in respect of this trip), and the refund is issued as a voucher, not cash [F2][NS-7].

Safety screen (SAFE-1/SAFE-2): I read every message, the driver's statement and the complaint. The chat is a rider ETA question [F7] and a driver traffic update [F8]; the statement [F10] and the complaint are factual summaries. No threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegations appear [F7][F8][F10]; safety_concern = none.

You cancelled about three minutes after your driver accepted, which is inside the free-cancellation window, so the fee shouldn't have applied. Your driver also never reached the pickup point or marked himself as arrived, so this was never treated as a no-show on your part. The $6.61 comes back as a Ryde voucher on your account. No action is being taken against your account, and nothing further is needed from you.

DRIVER: We've reviewed the disputed cancellation fee on this trip and refunded the $6.61 to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The deciding point is that the rider cancelled about three minutes after you accepted, which falls inside the free-cancellation window, so no cancellation fee applied. Your distance from the pickup point and traffic conditions didn't change that outcome. This is a fare adjustment only — no action is being taken against your account and no penalty applies. You'll see this reflected in your trip records.
